newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Idemitsu to buy 900,000 bbls Iraq crude.
newsitem.headline: Japan Idemitsu to buy 900,000 bbls Iraq crude.

text.p: Refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Thursday it had signed an agreement with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) to buy 900,000 barrels of mid-April loading Iraqi crude.
The contract with SOMO was signed on March 23, and has been approved by the United Nations, an Idemitsu spokesman said.
Idemitsu has agreed to buy Iraq's Basrah Light crude at a price of five cents per barrel above the average of Oman and Dubai quotations, a company spokesman said.

The Iraqi crude will be loaded at the Gulf Port of Mina al-Bakr in mid-April and is due to reach Japan in early May, the spokesman said. However, it is not yet clear which refinery will process the crude, he said.
Iraq is currently selling oil in the second 90-day period of its six-month oil-for-food deal, which started on December 10 and will end on June 7.

Under the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude over six months, mainly to buy food and medicine for civilians suffering under sanctions slapped on Baghdad after it invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
Earlier this month, Cosmo Oil Co Ltd said it had agreed with SOMO to buy 900,000 barrels of Basrah Light crude for April 10 to 25 loading.
Last December, trading house Mitsubishi Corp signed an agreement to buy Iraqi crude on behalf of five Japanese oil firms. The contract is for 20,000 barrels-per-day over a period of six months.
